newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks pick up steam at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks pick up steam at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks pushed higher at the close in heavy turnover Wednesday fuelled by Wall Street's run to record highs, dealers said.

"Today was a good day for all the big Latin American markets which rallied along with the Dow," said Emilio Alessandro of brokers Alessandro. "The sweeping recovery gave local players confidence and bolstered the timid advance we saw Monday and Tuesday."
The blue-chip MerVal index climbed 1.5 percent to close at session highs of 718.52, stretching gains so far this week to 2.2 percent.
"The MerVal has overcome resistance at 715 and is aiming for its second historical record of 728 (set February 16, 1994)," another trader said.
Floor volume swelled to 37.9 million pesos from an already strong tally of 31.8 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter deals totaled 133 million pesos against 107.1 million Tuesday.
"Business was brisk but this could pose a problem Thursday, because unless cash flows stay strong the bolsa might not be able to soak up profit-taking," Alessandro said.
Traders noted ADRs drove the rally with strong gains in the heavyweight telephone, oil and bank sectors.
However, they said these sectors could be restrained by next week's large options expirations.
The broad market index closed up 1.7 percent, with winners smashing losers 55 to 14 and nine issues closing flat.

No main-tier issues posted losses. Best MerVal performers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, construction stock Polledo and steelmaker Acindar, which closed up 3.1 percent, 3.0 percent and 2.9 percent, respectively.
Among second-line stocks petrochemical concern Atanor shot up 7.4 percent and Banco del Suquia rose 6.0 percent.
